title: Filtered aquatic small tubular mesh-bottomed containers (FAST-MC): A low-cost, efficient method for rearing zebrafish larvae in filtered water
author: Caballero, Robles, et al.

steps.title: Prepare experimental aquarium
steps.instruction: Fill a 40‑L aquarium with system water (same water used for adult stock tanks). Install a top filter whose intake is covered with black mesh to keep large debris out, and place a submersible heater set to maintain 28–29 °C for the duration of the experiment.

steps.title: Build PVC float for FAST‑MC
steps.instruction: Cut 3 in (76 mm) long, ¾ in (19 mm) diameter PVC pipe pieces to the desired length and connect them with 90° elbow fittings (19 mm inner diameter) to form a square float; optionally add T‑connectors to hold two hatcheries. Hand‑tighten all fittings (no PVC glue or other adhesive). Verify that the assembled float is watertight before use.

steps.title: Assemble mesh‑bottom hatchery
steps.instruction: Use a clear acrylic cylinder (102 mm diameter, 115 mm tall) closed on one end with 400 µm nylon mesh. Affix the mesh to the cylinder with aquarium‑grade silicone and let dry overnight. Place a black rubber “O”‑ring around the outside of the cylinder 13 mm (0.5 in) from the open (non‑mesh) side. Insert the hatchery into the PVC holder so the O‑ring rests on the PVC float; adjust the O‑ring as needed to secure the hatchery.

steps.title: Install FAST‑MC apparatus in aquarium
steps.instruction: Place the assembled PVC float with the mesh‑bottom hatchery (or two hatcheries) into the 40‑L aquarium, ensuring it remains watertight. Secure the apparatus to the aquarium side by threading airline tubing through the corners (between hatchery and float) on both sides and clipping the tubing to the aquarium with binder clips. Cover the aquarium with its lid to prevent evaporation. Allow the entire set‑up to sit undisturbed for one day to confirm proper function.

steps.title: Add eggs or larvae
steps.instruction: Introduce fertilized zebrafish eggs and/or larvae (6–10 per container) into each mesh‑bottom FAST‑MC container. Use either system water or experimental water containing chemicals, depending on the treatment design.

steps.title: Monitor water quality
steps.instruction: Routinely measure temperature, pH, ammonia, nitrate, and nitrite in each aquarium. Add fresh water weekly to compensate for evaporative loss. For FAST‑MC containers, no daily water changes are required because the top filter continuously circulates water.

steps.title: Perform routine maintenance
steps.instruction: If using petri‑dish controls, change 25–30 % of the water daily to remove uneaten food, debris, and dead larvae. For FAST‑MC containers, add water to the aquarium approximately once a week; during this weekly addition, remove any uneaten food that has fallen through the mesh bottom of the hatchery.

steps.title: Clean and reuse components
steps.instruction: After larvae are removed, separate the aquarium, filter, and FAST‑MC apparatus and clean all parts according to the fish facility’s standard protocols. Reuse all components if system water was used. If experimental chemical water was used, consider restricting reuse to avoid cross‑contamination.

steps.title: Seal and leach PVC float if needed
steps.instruction: If the hand‑tightened PVC float is not watertight, apply PVC glue or another sealant, then soak and/or wash the glued float several times to leach out any potentially harmful chemicals before reuse.
